fullPassage: When social scientists discovered that the magnitude of income inequality in a country or region predicted some outcomes that a family's average income did not, economists invented an index of income inequality called the Gini coefficient. A Gini coefficient of 0 means that everyone in the society has the same income; a coefficient of 1.0 means that one family earns all the income. The Gini coefficient can also be used to index inequality in total wealth. The coefficients in most contemporary societies range from 0.3 to 0.6. Canada, Japan, and the Scandinavian countries have low coefficients (less than 0.3); South Africa, Brazil, Nigeria, and China have the highest (from 0.4 to 0.6). The Gini coefficient for the United States in 2013 was a moderately high 0.45, compared with 0.38 in 1950, which implies that 10 percent of Americans in 2013 owned more than two-thirds of the country's wealth. The Gini coefficient for the United States was much lower two hundred years earlier when most families owned a house and livestock, and a college education was a less important requirement for accumulating wealth. The currently high level of inequality is accompanied by an imbalance in the degree of influence on legislation. Two social scientists report in Perspectives on Politics that between 1981 and 2002, close to one-half of the laws Congress passed were favored by a small proportion of very wealthy Americans. By contrast, only 18 percent of the proposals a majority of the public favored, but the wealthy opposed, became law.

questions.passage: When social scientists discovered that the magnitude of income inequality in a country or region predicted some outcomes that a family's average income did not, economists invented an index of income inequality called the Gini coefficient. A Gini coefficient of 0 means that everyone in the society has the same income; a coefficient of 1.0 means that one family earns all the income. The Gini coefficient can also be used to index inequality in total wealth. The coefficients in most contemporary societies range from 0.3 to 0.6. Canada, Japan, and the Scandinavian countries have low coefficients (less than 0.3); South Africa, Brazil, Nigeria, and China have the highest (from 0.4 to 0.6). The Gini coefficient for the United States in 2013 was a moderately high 0.45, compared with 0.38 in 1950, which implies that 10 percent of Americans in 2013 owned more than two-thirds of the country's wealth. The Gini coefficient for the United States was much lower two hundred years earlier when most families owned a house and livestock, and a college education was a less important requirement for accumulating wealth. The currently high level of inequality is accompanied by __________. Two social scientists report in Perspectives on Politics that between 1981 and 2002, close to one-half of the laws Congress passed were favored by a small proportion of very wealthy Americans. By contrast, only 18 percent of the proposals a majority of the public favored, but the wealthy opposed, became law.

questions.stem:
주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?

When social scientists discovered that the magnitude of income inequality in a country or region predicted some outcomes that a family's average income did not, economists invented an index of income inequality called the Gini coefficient. A Gini coefficient of 0 means that everyone in the society has the same income; a coefficient of 1.0 means that one family earns all the income. The Gini coefficient can also be used to index inequality in total wealth.

(A) The Gini coefficient for the United States in 2013 was a moderately high 0.45, compared with 0.38 in 1950, which implies that 10 percent of Americans in 2013 owned more than two-thirds of the country's wealth.

(B) The coefficients in most contemporary societies range from 0.3 to 0.6. Canada, Japan, and the Scandinavian countries have low coefficients (less than 0.3); South Africa, Brazil, Nigeria, and China have the highest (from 0.4 to 0.6).

(C) The Gini coefficient for the United States was much lower two hundred years earlier when most families owned a house and livestock, and a college education was a less important requirement for accumulating wealth.

det.analysis:
❌ ① (A)-(B)-(C): (A)는 2013년 미국의 구체적 수치를 다루는데, 이에 앞서 '대부분의 사회들의 계수 범위(0.3~0.6)'를 설명하는 (B)가 먼저 나와야 자연스러움
✅ ② (B)-(A)-(C): (B) 여러 사회의 일반적인 계수 범위와 국가별 비교 제시 → (A) 그중 미국의 2013년 구체적 수치로 범위를 좁힘 → (C) '200년 전' 비교를 위해서는 (A)의 '현재' 수치가 먼저 제시되어야 함 ←정답
❌ ③ (B)-(A)-(C)와 동일한 조합 아님 — 중복 제거
❌ ④ (C)-(A)-(B): (C)는 '더 낮았다(much lower)'는 비교 표현으로 시작하는데, 비교 대상인 (A)의 2013년 수치가 먼저 제시되지 않으면 무엇과 비교하는지 알 수 없음
det.tip: (C)의 'much lower'는 비교급이므로 비교 기준이 되는 (A)의 구체적 수치(2013년 0.45)가 앞서 나와야 함

The Gini coefficient for the United States was much lower two hundred years earlier when most families owned a house and livestock, and a college education was a less important requirement for accumulating wealth. The currently high level of inequality is accompanied by an imbalance in the degree of influence on legislation. Two social scientists report in Perspectives on Politics that between 1981 and 2002, close to one-half of the laws Congress passed were favored by a small proportion of very wealthy Americans. By contrast, only 18 percent of the proposals a majority of the public favored, but the wealthy opposed, became law.
